haiku-low.q1: The server checks permission, validates the view and reads reports.row_count. At 10,000 rows or fewer it returns the CSV as the click's response. Above that it records an export, queues a job and returns 202 JSON.
haiku-low.q2: The server returns the existing active export with 202 and its own filters and columns. No second export is created. If the filters differ, the page says so.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the stored file 7 days after creation. No cleanup job exists.
haiku-low.q4: Three attempts, with retries after 60 s and 300 s. After the third failure the row is marked failed, the slot is freed, and a failure email is sent.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. All report_rows reads go there, never the primary. The App DB primary holds only the report_exports state table.
haiku-low.q6: In the App DB table report_exports. The page polls every 5 seconds while queued or running, pausing when hidden. Reopening the page fetches the current state from the status endpoint.
haiku-low.q7: It streams rows in 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica, encodes them and uploads 8 MB multipart parts. Estimated peak is about 30 MB, under the 100 MB target, pending benchmark.
haiku-low.q8: Each failed attempt's upload is aborted best-effort, and unfinished uploads expire after 24 hours. The next attempt starts from the first row under a new key. The resumable fallback is not built unless the benchmark requires it.
haiku-low.q9: They are kept in the report_exports row as a validated copy of filters and cols. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job reads the filters and columns from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The database enforces one active export, so the losing insert is rejected.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be complete and the row's done update must succeed, recording object_key, before the email is sent. A rerun on a done export sends the email only if notified_at is empty.
haiku-low.q12: Nothing is sent until the CSV is complete, so the user gets no partial file. A replica error returns 500. Nothing is stored, so there is no state to clean up.

sonnet.q1: By reports.row_count: 10,000 rows or fewer is the small path, where the click's response is the CSV itself (200, text/csv, saved as a file), with nothing stored and no job. More than 10,000 is the large path: the server records an export, queues a background job and returns HTTP 202 with JSON {export_id, status, created_at, filters, cols}. Later the job emails a 24-hour link. A stale row_count on a small report can also produce a 202.
sonnet.q2: The unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') rejects the second insert. The server loads the existing export and runs reclaim on it. If reclaim finds the job lost, it fails that export and the insert is retried once. Otherwise it returns the existing export with 202 and the same JSON shape (including its filters and cols). No new export is created. If the filters differ from this click's, the page says 'An export with different filters is already in progress'.
sonnet.q3: The emailed link is a signed_url of 86400 s, so 24 hours. It keeps working for those 24 hours whatever happens to the user's access. The stored file is deleted by the bucket's existing lifecycle rule 7 days after the object is created. No cleanup job is built. The in-app Download button uses a fresh 5-minute link. A done export is hidden from the page 6 days after finished_at, and the download endpoint returns 410 after that.
sonnet.q4: Three attempts: the queue retries after 60 s, then 300 s. After attempt 3 fails, on_final_failure runs once. It calls fail(id, 'export failed'), which sets the row to failed, sets error and finished_at, and frees the user's slot. It then sends the 'report_export_failed' email with the report name. The page shows the failed status. If the row was already done, because the email step was what failed, it only logs. Email errors in the handler are caught and logged.
sonnet.q5: The read replica, never the primary, for all report_rows reads. Export state lives in the App DB (the primary application database). The reports.row_count read uses the same connection and query as the page does today. It is treated as metadata, and the plan flags this as an assumption to confirm.
sonnet.q6: Status is stored in the report_exports table in the App DB. The page learns of changes by polling GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/current every 5 seconds while the status is queued or running (paused while the tab is hidden, stopped on done or failed). On page load it fetches the same endpoint, so a returning user sees the current state. That endpoint checks report.view and returns 403 without it. It hides done exports older than 6 days, and other states older than 7 days. It also applies reclaim rule 3, so a lost job shows as failed.
sonnet.q7: By streaming. The job reads the replica with keyset pagination in pages of 5,000 rows and encodes each row into a byte buffer. When the buffer reaches 8 MB it calls upload_part (S3-style multipart upload) and clears the buffer. The remainder goes as the last part, and complete_multipart then publishes the file. About 113 parts for a 900 MB file. Estimated peak memory is about 30 MB (design target under 100 MB, limit 512 MB). A benchmark in 9.1 must confirm both memory and the 900 s time target.
sonnet.q8: Nothing is visible at the key until complete_multipart, so partial data is never downloadable. On an exception the attempt calls abort_multipart (best effort) and re-raises. If the worker is killed, the bucket discards the unfinished multipart upload after 24 hours. The next attempt starts from the beginning, with a new upload at its own key ({report_id}/{id}-{attempt}.csv), because the queue keeps no progress. The exception is the optional resumable fallback, built only if the benchmark fails the time target. There a retry resumes at row_id > resume_row_id with the saved etags.
sonnet.q9: The page URL holds the view and the server stores nothing about it. The click sends the filters and cols, and the server validates them with the rows API's parser. It then copies them into the filters and cols columns of the report_exports row (App DB). The enqueue payload is only {export_id}. The job reads filters and cols from that row, which is the single source of truth.
sonnet.q10: The database does, through a unique partial index on report_exports (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running'). Of two racing inserts, one is rejected, and the loser returns the existing export.
sonnet.q11: Before the email: the multipart upload must have completed (complete_multipart), and the row must have been updated to done with object_key (conditional on status running and its attempt). The email is sent only if notified_at is empty, and notified_at is set after sending. If the queue runs the job again and the row is already done, step 5.1 skips straight to 6.2. It sends the email only if notified_at is empty and does nothing more. If the row is failed or not found, it just returns. If the same attempt is delivered twice, the second claim changes 0 rows and it returns. The one remaining risk is a death between sending and recording notified_at, which may give one duplicate email.
sonnet.q12: A replica error returns HTTP 500. The CSV is built fully in an in-memory buffer and is sent only when complete, so the user never receives a partial file. Nothing is stored. The button shows an error and can be clicked again.
